answer.rationale: With 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% with no buffer, switching primary vendor is the only clear path to the mandated 18% cut but carries unacceptable delivery risk; adding a second source protects supply but does not meet the near-term spend cut and may raise cost. Incumbent renewal alone preserves continuity but likely locks current pricing after refusal. I intend to use the expiry as leverage to negotiate non-unit-price TCO terms—rebates, payment terms, freight/VMI, scrap/warranty sharing, volume bands, and short extension—while explicitly avoiding a primary-source move this cycle. I want c2 checked for hidden switching/risk costs behind the low-cost win and c4 checked for whether incumbent movement required formal renewal leverage rather than ad hoc price reopening.
